Module Overview

Please make sure to read these modules in their entirety to make sure you’re all set to have a successful Ship 30 experience.

Dear Shipper,

Welcome aboard Ship 30 for 30: The Main Port To The Creator Economy!

We are so excited to have you onboard, and hope you are ready to set sail.

The Ship 30 for 30 program is designed to give you everything you need to become a prolific, popular, and profitable creator in the digital world.

And the best part?

We’re going to help you do that in just 30 days.

But before we leave the main port and head for open waters, there’s some housekeeping we need to do to make sure you’re setup for success!

So in this module, we’re going to walk you through:

  • How Ship 30 for 30 works

  • How to update your Skool profile

  • How to navigate our Ship 30 Skool community

  • And everything you’re going to learn throughout your entire Ship 30 experience!

But before we dive into any of this good stuff, there’s a CRUCIAL action item you need to complete!

[ACTION ITEM] Download The Ship 30 Course Guide

We've created a printable Ship 30 Course Guide that's going to give you a daily list of action items to complete between now and the end of Ship 30 for 30.

To download it, click on one of the links below (you can download it in your preferred format) and save the file to your computer! (We recommend printing it out and keeping it on your desk!)

  • Download the Ship 30 Course Guide as a Google Doc

  • Download the Ship 30 Course Guide as a Notion doc

  • Download the Ship 30 Course Guide as a docx file

  • Download the Ship 30 Course Guide as a PDF

Once you’ve downloaded the Course Guide in your preferred format, you’re all set to dive into today’s Onboarding Week Module.


🔹Lesson #1: How Ship 30 Works

We’ve carefully designed Ship 30 for 30 to help you write & publish one piece of content (more specifically, an Atomic Essay) every day for 30 days.

But before you start writing & publishing your Atomic Essays every day, you need to complete our 5 Onboarding Week Modules.

Throughout these modules, we will walk you through everything you need to know and have in place in order to:

  • Build your daily writing habit & set your creative constraints

  • Create, design, and launch your very own Social Blog

  • Introduce yourself to the Ship 30 community

  • And get ready to set sail!

And just so you can plan and block time appropriately, each of these modules will take you 15-20 minutes to complete (and all of them have some sort of action item).

Now, there’s 2 “ways” you can go about completing our Onboarding Week modules:

  1. [RECOMMENDED] You can complete one Onboarding Week module per day across 5 consecutive days. We recommend this approach because it’s a great way to gradually start building your Daily Writing Habit & practice your “Sacred Hours” (which is a concept we will introduce you to in the next module).

  2. You can complete all 5 Onboarding Week module in just one day. If you’re eager to get started shipping (and have the time & energy to binge all our Onboarding Modules in one sitting), by all means go for it.

Our only advice?

Avoid anything in between!

Now, let’s take a quick look at how our Ship 30 Skool Community is setup—so you can easily navigate it, find our curriculum resources, and connect with other Shippers.


🔹Lesson #2: How To Navigate Skool

One of the biggest reasons why we decided to use Skool to host our Ship 30 community is because it’s extremely simple and intuitive to use.

There’s really only 5 main “places” or sections in the entire Skool group:

  • The Community Section. This is essentially the community “feed.” From here, you can both make your own posts, and read & engage with the posts of other Ship 30 members. Now, within our community “feed,” we’ve also created a handful of “post categories” to keep posts and conversations organized. These are super straightforward—but don’t worry, we’ll give you a quick rundown of each category in one of our upcoming modules.

  • The Classroom Section. Here’s where you can find all the Ship 30 for 30 Curriculum Modules, templates, and bonus resources that you unlocked when you hopped aboard. We’ve put a lot of time and effort to make sure this section is organized in a such a way that you can easily find anything you need or want to dig into as you go through Ship 30.

  • The Calendar Section. As you know, Ship 30 for 30 is a self-paced program. However, from time to time, we might host special events and live sessions. And whenever we do, we will let you know and add those events to our Calendar Section so you don't miss them!

  • The Members Section. From here, you can easily find a list of all the other members in the Ship 30 for 30 community. Using the Skool “search bar,” you can look up certain words or phrases to find other members who might be interested in the same topics or who might live in the same city as you do. Don’t worry, we’ll also share a few pro tips to help you meet and connect with other Shippers shortly.

  • The Leaderboards Section. Last but not least, from the Leaderboards section you’ll be able to see a list of our most engaged Ship 30 for 30 community members. Full transparency: We haven’t been able to fully set up this yet. But we definitely plan on adding exclusive rewards and bonuses that you can unlock after you’ve reached a certain “engagement level.”

But now that you know all the ins and outs of how our Ship 30 Skool community is structured, let’s make sure your Skool profile is all setup for success.


🔹Lesson #3: Updating Your Skool Profile

In order to create your Skool account, you had to upload a profile picture and a short bio.

However, there’s a few other “fields” you should update in your Skool profile in order to make it easier for other community members to find you and engage with you!

So, let’s get you setup.

How To Get Your Skool Profile Setup For Success

  1. Head over to this link so you can open your Skool settings

  2. If you haven’t already, fill in your Bio section. (An easy template you can follow for your Bio: “{Job role/occupation} at {Company name/institution}. Writing about {topic}, {topic}, and {topic}.”

  3. Fill in the “Location” field with the name of the city you currently live in (especially if you’re interested in connecting and meeting up with other Shippers who might live near you!)

  4. Lastly, if you’d also like to connect with other Shippers on Twitter and LinkedIn (or wherever you’re planning on writing throughout Ship 30), be sure to add your social links too!

Boom—and just like that, your Skool profile is all set!

Now, let’s take a look at the curriculum—so you can get preview of everything you’re going to learn over the coming weeks!


🔹Lesson #4: Curriculum Overview

Alright—now that we’ve taken care of all the logistics, let’s take a quick look at everything you’re going to learn over the next couple of weeks.

The day after officially completing our Onboarding Week Modules, you will begin shipping your daily Atomic Essays.

But Ship 30 for 30 is so much more than just a “daily writing a challenge.”

It’s an entire masterclass teaching you the fundamentals of Digital Writing.

(Which is very different from legacy “English class” writing.)

So instead of just talking at you (like a boring English professor), Ship 30 for 30 forces you to put your learnings into practice IMMEDIATELY by writing and publishing Atomic Essays (and other pieces of short-form content) every day for 30 days.

Here’s a quick overview of everything we’re going to cover:

  • [Mindset Of A Digital Writer] Day 1: The Anatomy of an Atomic Essay

  • [Mindset Of A Digital Writer] Day 2: (EIG) 2-Year Test

  • [Mindset Of A Digital Writer] Day 3: (EIG) FOR WHO/SO THAT

  • [Mindset Of A Digital Writer] Day 4: (EIG) Personal Credibility vs Borrowed Credibility

  • [Mindset Of A Digital Writer] Day 5: (EIG) The 4A Framework

  • [Mindset Of A Digital Writer] Day 6: (EIG) 30 Proven Approaches

  • [Mindset Of A Digital Writer] Day 7: The Lean Writing Framework

  • [Headlines & Hooks] Day 8: Irresistible Headlines Part I

  • [Headlines & Hooks] Day 9: Irresistible Headlines Part II

  • [Headlines & Hooks] Day 10: Irresistible Headlines Part III

  • [Headlines & Hooks] Day 11: Twist The Knife

  • [Headlines & Hooks] Day 12: 5 Proven Headline Styles

  • [Headlines & Hooks] Day 13: X/Twitter Hooks

  • [Headlines & Hooks] Day 14: LinkedIn Hooks

  • [Flawless Formatting] Day 15: Prep The Page

  • [Flawless Formatting] Day 16: Single-Sentence Openers

  • [Flawless Formatting] Day 17: The Art of Subheads

  • [Flawless Formatting] Day 18: 1/3/1 Writing Rhythms

  • [Flawless Formatting] Day 19: Formatting Short-Form Content

  • [Flawless Formatting] Day 20: Formatting X (Twitter) Threads

  • [Flawless Formatting] Day 21: Formatting LinkedIn Posts

  • [Analytics & Category Creation] Day 22: Make Noise, Listen For Signal

  • [Analytics & Category Creation] Day 23: 5 Data Points

  • [Analytics & Category Creation] Day 24: Doubling-Down On Proven Topics

  • [Analytics & Category Creation] Day 25: Doubling-Down On Proven Audiences

  • [Analytics & Category Creation] Day 26: Doubling-Down On Proven Narratives

  • [Analytics & Category Creation] Day 27: Rewriting Your X (Twitter) Bio

  • [Analytics & Category Creation] Day 28: Rewriting Your LinkedIn Bio

  • [Analytics & Category Creation] Day 29: Pinning Your Best Work

  • [Analytics & Category Creation] Day 30: Building Your Idea File (6-Month Content Strategy)

In a nutshell, we will help you build all the skills you need to leverage your daily writing habit into digital products, courses, career acceleration, and other monetization opportunities…

All while building your library of content, gathering signal about your niche, making friends, and growing an audience.

Full Stack Writer

But Ship 30 for 30 is only the beginning.

(So if you’re thinking, “Ok… I start writing online. Then what?” Don’t worry, we’re here to help.)

After you complete 30 days of shipping, you will unlock the option to hop aboard our more advanced writing program, Full-Stack Writer, where we show you how to:

  • All the different ways you can monetize your writing

  • Create irresistible offers & landing pages that sell

  • Build a scalable newsletter in your niche

  • Launch digital products ($$$$)

  • And more.

This is for alumni of Ship 30 for 30 ONLY.

The reason we make Ship 30 for 30 a pre-requisite for joining Full-Stack Writer is because we can talk about monetization all day long, but if you don’t have your daily writing habit in place, if you aren’t consistently creating content online, if you don’t have the fundamentals down, then none of it will matter. And we only want to work with people who have proven they are committed by building that foundation, first.

So, once you complete Ship 30 for 30 (even if you don’t ship every single day, as long as you complete the course), you will be invited to join Full-Stack Writer.

So... are you ready?

Here's the last (and most important thing) we want to share before you get started:

You get out of Ship 30 for 30 what you put in.

If you write every single day, engage heavily with the community, and put into practice everything we’re going to share with you throughout the program, we can confidently say Ship 30 will change your life (and will completely change your trajectory as a Digital Writer and Creator).

And don't worry—it can seem like a lot at first.

But as we get going, you'll find the right workflow for you!

What’s next?

  • If you decided to take the “recommended” path (and complete one Onboarding Week module per day for 5 days), then you’re all set for today. Just make sure to set a reminder and block some time to go through the next Onboarding Week module tomorrow. (And don’t worry, we’ll share with you some extra tips & frameworks for doing that effectively throughout Ship 30 tomorrow!)

  • If you decided to take the “accelerated” path (and complete all Onboarding Week modules in just one day), you can use this link to dive into Module #2.

No matter what approach you choose, though, make sure to click complete today’s assignment before you move on!

records.content:
Module Overview

Ahoy, and welcome to Onboarding Week Module #2!

In this module, we’re going to walk you through the 3 keys to building a Daily Writing Habit:

  • Creating (not finding) your “Sacred Hours”

  • Setting your creative constraints

  • And not missing twice.

Ready?

Let’s dive in!

🔹Lesson #1: 3 Keys To Build A Daily Writing Habit

Writing and publishing every day for 30 days will change your life.

We say that at the beginning of every Shipper’s journey because we mean it.

If you write every day for 30 days, engage with the community, and put into practice what we’re going to share with you, you will walk away with:

  • A daily writing habit

  • A clearer, calmer mind

  • Confidence in your abilities

  • 30 pieces of published content

  • A foundation for months of future writing

  • Lifelong friendships with like-minded people

  • The frameworks, skills, and techniques to flourish as an online writer

The Challenge Ahead

Over 10,000 writers have built a daily writing habit through Ship 30 for 30.

And all of them faced the same 10 struggles at the beginning of the program:

  1. Distractions

  2. Over-editing

  3. Perfectionism

  4. Procrastination

  5. Self-confidence

  6. Generating ideas

  7. Impostor syndrome

  8. Writing consistently

  9. Choosing a platform

  10. Finding time to write

We bet you can point to some, if not all, of these problems as reasons your writing habit has been shaky.

Luckily, Ship 30 for 30 is designed to help solve every single one of these problems.

And by acknowledging these struggles, you can build an intentional writing habit and workflow that crushes them one by one.

In the sections that follow, we'll help you build this workflow step by step.

However, we want to warn you..

The workflow you design on the first day of the challenge will be the workflow you most likely repeat for all 30 days.

This is a blessing and a curse.

If you are mindful about setting up your workflow beforehand, the challenge is easy.

But if you start haphazardly, you will struggle and eventually fall off.

So, let's be intentional about creating your writing workflow.

The 3 Keys To Build Your Daily Writing Habit

Daily Writing Habit Key #1: Creating (Not "Finding") Your Sacred Hours

"I just can't find the time to write.”

The truth is, people don't "find" the time to write. Just like you don't try to "find time" to see your significant other, and you don't try to "find time" to go to the gym, or see your old friend from college with they are in town, or see your parents on Christmas. When something matters to you, you MAKE the time.

And then you organize the rest of your day around the thing you decided to make the time to do.

So, that's what you need to do, first and foremost, to build a sustainable daily writing habit.

To write every day for 30 days, you need to CREATE time in advance.

We call these your "Sacred Hours": the time of day that is set aside to write.

Sacred hours are blocked off chunks of time that are, you guessed it, sacred.

  • Unreachable.

  • No distractions.

  • Fully off the grid.

  • Defended ruthlessly.

Just you and your work for at least an hour.

To find your sacred hours, there are two questions to answer:

  • What time of day am I most productive?

  • What time of day can I be least responsive?

This will be different for everyone in every circumstance.

If you are a college student, your sacred hours are going to be different than someone who works full time, versus someone juggling work and kids, versus someone who is retired. What matters is that you find the time of day that works best for you. Then, once your sacred hours are chosen, send yourself a calendar invite.

Treat this hour as a meeting with yourself (that you can't cancel!).

Defend this hour ruthlessly.

Let no one intrude on your sacred hours.

If you do this, you will not only succeed in the Ship 30 for 30 writing program, but you will create the foundation for a life-changing habit.

Daily Writing Habit Key #2: Setting Your Constraints

The second step of building your daily writing habit is setting your constraints.

Creativity thrives with intentional constraints.

Where writers go wrong is they task themselves with sitting in front of a blank page and "making magic happen" on a whim.

But we all know that's a recipe for failure. Instead, Ship 30 for 30 is designed with a handful of constraints in mind so that you don't experience the feeling of having "too many options," and instead can just focus on writing & publishing a 250-word Atomic Essay, on a single idea, every day for 30 days.

And if this is your first time writing an Atomic Essay, don’t worry—we’ll walk you through everything you need to write your first Atomic Essay over the next few days!

Here are the Atomic Essays constraints we recommend:

  • Time: You have 30-60 minutes to write. This will take longer in the beginning, but you will get faster! Then, 5-10 minutes MAX to edit. (A quick glance for grammar and punctuation is about all you should be focusing on.)

  • Topic: This is 100% up to you, and we'll walk you through how to set your topic constraints.

  • Length: Your Atomic Essay should be no more than 300 words. This forces you to think clearly, concisely, and deliver your point effectively.

  • Platform: You will publish every day for 30 days to Twitter and your Typeshare Social Blog (more on that tomorrow!)

  • Cadence: This one is easy. You will write and publish every day for 30 days.

  • Environment: This is about writing in the same place, at the same time, every day.

The recommended constraints are tight for a reason. They stop you from overthinking, over editing, and falling out of practice.

They force you to SHIP, which is the goal of Ship 30 for 30.

If you stick to these constraints, Ship 30 for 30 will be a ton of fun (and you will have covered an incredible amount of ground by the time you're done).

Finally, we encourage you to craft a "Daily Writing" promise statement for how you will write for the next 30 days.

Instead of setting the goal of "I am going to start writing every day," craft a statement that combines all of your constraints.

For example: "I am going to write every day for 60 minutes at 7 AM while sitting at my living room table. I will write 250-word Atomic Essays about productivity and mindfulness, published on Twitter and to my Social Blog."

Daily Writing Habit Key #3: Not Missing Twice

At Ship 30, our goal is to help you write & publish an Atomic Essay every day for 30 days.

But the truth is, shipping every single day is hard.

Sometimes life can get in the way and missing a day becomes inevitable—even if you’ve followed all our suggestions.

And that’s okay.

But whenever you miss a day, get right back onboard the day after—and NEVER miss twice.

Because the moment you miss 2 days in a row, that’s when your ship starts to lose momentum—and you run the risk of getting overboard.

So, remember:

Shipping most days >>>>> never shipping anything.

Progress over perfection.

Module Overview

Ahoy, and welcome to Onboarding Week Module #3!

In this module, we’re going to walk you through:

  • Why you should NOT start a blog

  • The best places to write online as a Digital Writer

  • And how to officially launch your Typeshare Social Blog

Ready to dive?

Let’s do it!


🔹Lesson #1: Don’t Start A Blog

Have you ever been given the advice to “start a blog?”

To be fair, this used to be the best way to publish your thoughts, insights, and stories online.

Back in the early days of the Internet, the only way to publish anything online was to either build your own website (blog) or write on someone else’s website (blog). And for a good ~10 years, this was an OK way of going about things.

But fast-forward to today, and starting your digital writing journey on a blog is the biggest mistake you could possibly make.

And here’s why.

Digital Writing 101

Blogs have one major flaw, and it’s something most writers aren’t aware of until much further along in their careers.

Your blog has no distribution flywheel.

A blog is just a website. So the big question is, how are people going to find out your website exists?

  • You’re going to have to tell them about it on social media.

  • You’re going to have to send it to your friends and family members via email.

  • You’re going to build an audience elsewhere and then say, “Hey, come check this thing out over here!”

The metaphor we like to use to illustrate how difficult it is to start a successful blog (and get people to read your writing there) goes like this: imagine you are downtown. Big city. Restaurants are full, bars have people walking in and out. Everyone is having a blast.

And there you show up, in your overalls and straw hat (legacy writers, gotta love ‘em) with a big sign.

PARTY AT MY HOUSE. 3 MILES AWAY IN A CORNFIELD.

Thousands of people walk straight past you. “Party at your house? 3 miles away? In a cornfield? Why? There’s dozens of restaurants and bars, and thousands of people right here?”

Long story short: nobody is going to come over.

That’s what it’s like starting a blog, and then asking readers on social platforms to come back to your house for a drink.

Which is why you are so much better off starting your digital writing journey by writing on social platforms.

  • Twitter

  • Quora

  • Medium

  • LinkedIn

Basically, anywhere readers already are.

When you write and publish content on social platforms, you are removing the single greatest obstacle in starting your own blog: finding readers! In fact, the way these social platforms are engineered is to, quite literally, serve your content up to as many people as possible who might be interested in what you have to say.

Of course, the big question people always ask is, “Well what if I have 0 followers?”

Ah, so glad you asked.

How these social platforms work actually has a lot less to do with how many followers you CURRENTLY have, and a lot more to do with how many people the platform thinks will be interested in your content.

For example, say you start writing about marketing, or writing advice, or how to grow a vegetable garden. Well, every time you hit “publish” on one of these social platforms, the algorithm is going to serve your content up to some readers it thinks might be interested in the topic you just wrote about. And if readers start engaging—reading, Liking, commenting, etc.—it’s going to serve it up to more readers. And more readers.

This is how some people with just a few hundred followers “go viral,” and end up getting hundreds of thousands of views (sometimes even millions of views) on their content.

Because the algorithm saw people liked what they had written, and decided to serve it up to more people.

The chances of this happening with your website/blog are slim to none.

“But what if I still want a blog because I want somewhere to store all my content?”

Ah, another great question.

If you really love the idea of having a centralized place for all your content, then what we recommend isn’t for you to start a legacy “blog.”

We recommend you start a Social Blog.

A Social Blog is a website where you can have both a master library of all your content (which you own), and simultaneously plug into other social platforms to further distribute your content (and gather analytics in the process).

That way, you get all the upside of publishing your ideas on social platforms—while still being able to build a “home” for all your writing.

So now that you know why we recommend using a Social Blog (instead of a regular blog), we’re going to walk you through, step by step, how to launch your own Social Blog using Typeshare.

Let’s do it!


🔹Lesson #2: Launching Your Social Blog

All throughout Ship 30 for 30, you will be using Typeshare to write & store your Atomic Essays.

(As a reminder, an Atomic Essay is a short, compressed essay that’s 250 words or less. And the reason why we write Atomic Essays is because they make it easy to learn the fundamentals of Digital Writing and build a sustainable daily writing habit. But don’t worry, we’ll show you exactly how to write your first Atomic Essay on your First Day of Shipping!)

Typeshare is our very own software product that allows you to:

  • Write your Atomic Essays. The Atomic Essay format is the easiest way to learn the fundamentals of Digital Writing: idea generation, hooks, headlines, and formatting.

  • Become a data-driven writer. Inside Typeshare is a comprehensive analytics dashboard showing you cumulative performance, progress, and all sorts of new content ideas (for you to write about) based on data. *Note: You may see Typeshare’s Analytics Dashboard under construction during this cohort, as we are making new upgrades based on Twitter’s API changes.

  • Use Templates to overcome the fear of the blank page. Typeshare's flagship feature is its vast library of Templates, which you can use to remove the friction of "starting," accelerate your writing speed & efficiency, and leverage proven formats and hooks to grab the reader's attention.

  • Launch your Social Blog. Finally, all of your Digital Writing has a home. Your Social Blog comes with its own unique link, and displays your entire master library of content.

And as a Ship 30 for 30 member, you get exclusive access to:

  • An extended 35-day trial of Typeshare Pro

  • And the official Ship 30 for 30 Template Pack (30 days of writing templates to help you write & publish every day for 30 days with ease).

Now, let's get you all setup for frictionless publishing online!

Before you start publishing your Atomic Essays on Twitter and/or LinkedIn, Step 0 is creating an account on Typeshare, opening your 30 Days of Shipping template pack, and sharing your Social Blog on Twitter.

This way, when someone discovers your writing, they can quickly take a look at your master library on your Social Blog.

So let’s get you setup!


🔸Lesson #2 — Step 1

Step #1: Log In/Sign Up For Your FREE Typeshare Account

Whether you already have a Typeshare account or you need to create one, click here to get started.

If you don't have a Typeshare account yet, we recommend signing up with your Twitter account. But ultimately you can use whichever email address you'd like—it does not need to be the same you use for your Twitter or LinkedIn account. This is how we verify you as a Shipper, giving you FREE access to Typeshare for the duration of the cohort.

🔸Lesson #2 — Step 2

Step #2: Claim Your Free Month Of Typeshare & Your "30 Days Of Shipping" Template Pack.

When signing up for Typeshare, please make sure you’ve used this unique link so that you can get FREE access to Typeshare for the duration of the cohort—and unlock your Ship 30 for 30 exclusive “30 Days Of Shipping” Template Pack!

After you've logged in/signed up, you'll see a page like the one below. Be sure to select “Claim Free Month” to unlock 35 days of Typeshare FREE.

Since Typeshare uses Stripe to process payments, you will need to use a credit card to start your Free Trial. And if you don’t want to continue using Typeshare after Ship 30 for 30, don’t worry—we send you a reminder with the option to cancel your account before billing. But we find many Shippers fall in love with Typeshare Templates and want to continue using them on their Digital Writing Journey!

After you’ve signed up, be sure to also select “Unlock Template Pack” to unlock your Ship 30 exclusive Template Pack: 30 Days Of Shipping!


🔸Lesson #2 — Step 3

Step #3: Reserve Your Social Blog Username, Connect To Twitter, And Write A Short Bio

Next, it’s time to reserve your Social Blog username.

In the upper right-hand corner, click your profile picture and in the dropdown menu and select "Settings." (If you select My Social Blog this will take you to the live version. But you need to set it up first!)

It will take you to this screen:

On this page you can:

  • Create your username

  • Write your bio

  • Select a profile photo for your Social Blog

  • And add links (like books or products) you want to attach to your Social Blog.

Just be sure to hit “Save!” after you’re done setting up your profile.

Next, on the left-hand side click "Theme."

This is where you can select the look & feel of your Social Blog:

Finally, let’s connect your Twitter & LinkedIn account:

Click on "Linked Accounts" on the left-hand side of this screen.﻿﻿Here you can:

  • Connect your Twitter/X account

  • Connect your LinkedIn account

This will make it easy to cross-post between platforms!


🔹Lesson #2 — Step 4

Step #4: Create Your "Social Blog Launch Post"

There’s nothing quite like public accountability!

A fun “challenge” we give Shippers is to make a post committing to writing & publishing for the next 30 days on Twitter/X—and letting people know what, specifically, you plan on writing about.

So, ﻿go ahead and grab the link to your Social Blog, and post on Twitter/X using this template:

Interested in {Topic 1}, {Topic 2}, {Topic 3}?

Over the next 30 days, I'll be writing 30 Atomic Essays.

Follow my Social Blog on @typeshare_co: [Link To Your Social Blog]

Like this:

To make this super easy for you, here’s a Click-To-Tweet link to have the template filled in for you.


🔹Lesson #2 — Step 5

Step #5: Pin your Social Blog to the top of your Twitter/X Profile

Finally, one you’ve made your Social Blog launch post on Twitter/X, click the 3 little dots in the upper right-hand corner of the Tweet to “Pin” it to the top of your profile.

Now, your Social Blog will be easily accessible by you and anyone reading your content throughout Ship 30!

It should look like this:

Once you do these steps, congrats!

You have set the foundation for your entire trajectory as a Digital Writer.

Now, everything you write online is part of this master library on your Social Blog, and your Social Blog is now connected to one of the fastest-spinning distribution flywheels on the Internet (Twitter/X and LinkedIn).

Next, we're going to walk you through the basics of Digital Writing, the Atomic Essay format, and why we are such big believers in using templates.

records.content:
Module Overview

Ahoy, and welcome to Onboarding Week Module #4!

In this module, we’re going to walk you through:

  • The basics of Digital Writing

  • What’s an Atomic Essay (and why we write them)

  • And why we’re such big believers is using templates

  • And not missing twice.

Ready?

Let’s dive in!

🔹Lesson #1: Atomic Essays 101

What is an Atomic Essay (and do why we write them)?

Over the course of 30 days, you are going to write & publish 30 Atomic Essays.

But, what is an Atomic Essay?

An Atomic Essay is a short, compressed essay of 250 words or less.

And the purpose of writing an Atomic Essay is to share 1 clear idea—small enough that you can come up with "something" to write about every day, but not so much that it feels like a burden (causing you to fall out of your daily writing habit).

The reason we use the Atomic Essay format as the foundation for Ship 30 for 30 is because it is the easiest way for writers to learn the fundamentals of Digital Writing:

  • Headlines: In order to get readers to read your writing, you first need to "hook" them with a clear (not clever) headline. And in Ship 30, we show you exactly how to do that—as well as which hooks are most likely to engage readers.

  • Introductions: Right away, at the very beginning of your Atomic Essay (or any other kind of writing), you need to tell the reader why they should trust you. What makes your point of view credible, valuable, and worth their time? This needs to happen in the introduction.

  • Main Points: Next, the reader is going to "skim" your writing. If your Main Points (organized and formatted neatly) speak to their wants, needs, questions, and interests, then they will read your writing. If not, they will give your writing a quick skim, decide it's "not for them," and move on.

  • Writing Rhythms: To keep the reader engaged, it's important to give them small milestones to look forward to all the way down the page. Long paragraphs are a no-no. And in Ship 30, we give you a handful of proven writing rhythms to not only make your writing more musical, but ensure you never lose the reader's attention.

  • Conclusions: And finally, how do you want the reader to feel at the end of your piece? How can you make sure you've delivered on the promise you made in your headline? The Atomic Essay format allows you to practice all 5 of these foundational pieces of all Digital Writing, every single day.

After the first 2 weeks of Ship 30, we then build on the fundamentals using other forms of Digital Writing.

Weeks 1 & 2 are focused on writing Atomic Essays so that you can practice these foundational pieces of all great Digital Writing.

Then, in Weeks 3 & 4, we will start to show you how to use these fundamentals to write engaging Twitter Threads & LinkedIn posts.

Each of these different formats is better suited for different types of content, and we show you which formats work best for which types of ideas.

🔹Lesson #2: The Ship 30 Template Pack

As a Shipper, you also have access to our "30 Days of Shipping" template pack.

(If you’re reading this, you should’ve unlocked your “30 Days of Shipping” template pack already. But if for some reason you haven’t, make sure to revisit our Onboarding Week Module 2 and do that now!)

Consider this your life jacket to make sure you never run out of ideas of things to write about!To find your pack, just click:

  • "Templates" on the navigation bar on the horizontal left-hand side of the screen.

  • Scroll down and you'll see "30 Days of Shipping."

  • Click "View Pack"

And here you'll never run out of things to write about!

Now, using this template pack and the prompts inside Typeshare is not a requirement for your Ship 30 for 30 experience.

However, it's there for you if you...

  • Wake up one morning and can't think of anything to write about.

  • Want to see what dozens and dozens of proven templates look like for prolific digital writers.

  • Want to alternate between practicing with a blank page & practicing with templates.

We are firm believers in using templates to increase the efficiency and quality of our output as Digital Writers & Creators. And the reason Typeshare has so many templates to choose from is because these are the exact same templates we use ourselves—and we want to share them with you.

🔹Lesson #3: Brainstorm Your First Week Of Topics

During the first few modules of our Ship 30 curriculum, we’ll arm you with dozens of frameworks to keep you from ever staring at a blank page again.

But if you’re itching to start generating ideas now, here’s a list to get you started.

Before we dive in, these ideas come straight from our “4A Framework” (which we’ll tell you all about as we dig into the curriculum).

The 4A framework says there are 4 types of content:

  • Actionable (here's how)

  • Analytical (here's what)

  • Aspirational (yes, you can)

  • Anthropological (here's why)

Every 1 of these 30 ideas falls into 1 of these buckets.

Again, don’t worry – we are going to cover ALL of this during the first week of the curriculum. We just wanted to share these ideas with you during Onboarding to get your creative juices flowing–because you’re going to need them!

Now let’s dive in:

  • Share 1 underrated tip for solving a certain problem.

  • Share 1 framework that helps you get something done in less time or with less stress.

  • Share the 1 piece of advice to you would give to a beginner in your field.

  • Share 1 software tool that helps you the most (that most people know nothing about).

  • Share 1 helpful website (that you think is rarely used).

  • Share a step-by-step guide for accomplishing 1 specific task.

  • Share the 1 book that most helped you in learning about your topic.

  • Share the 1 podcast you listen to religiously – and what others will learn from it.

  • Share the 1 Twitter thread you've bookmarked and reread multiple times – and what you learned from it.

  • Share the 1 blog post that once you read, permanently changed the way you see the world.

  • (Alright – those were all actionable. Now let's dig into Aspirational)

  • Share 1 mistake you made as a beginner – and what you learned from it.

  • Share the single most valuable thing you learned from a mentor.

  • Share your personal story – where you used to be, where you are now, and how you got here.

  • Share 1 piece of advice to your 5-years-ago self.

  • Share 1 common trait of the people you look up to.

  • Share 1 quote you live by – where you found it, and how it impacts you.

  • Share your personal playbook – how you achieved some result and the steps you took to get there.

  • Share 1 trend you’ve noticed and what it means for your topic

  • Share 1 number behind your business and why it’s important

  • Share 1 reason why 1 of your core beliefs is true

  • Share 1 thing you believe that everyone else doesn’t – and why you’re correct

  • Share 1 (uncommon) observation you have about the world – and why others are missing it

  • Share 1 razor (decision-making framework) you use in your day-to-day life

Now—you might be thinking “why are all of these just ‘1’ idea instead of 4 or 5 or 10?”

Because as explained earlier, Ship 30 is about writing “Atomic” pieces of content.

To write every day for 30 days, you have to start small.

This means keeping things sustainable—instead of sharing 10 mistakes, just share most important one. Instead of sharing 10 tips, just share the most valuable one. Instead of sharing 10 quotes, share the most-lifechanging one.

So hopefully this list does 2 things:

  1. Gets your creative juices flowing, with each idea leading to another idea and on and on

  2. Helps you realize that writing every day for 30 days is 100% possible—when you’re working from a well of ideas (which we will do everything possible to make sure you have!)

Now, if you STILL aren't sure what to write about, don’t worry!

Here’s YET another tool to help you start generating ideas:

AI-Powered Endless Idea Generator

Inside Typeshare, we’ve also created an automated version of the Endless Idea Generator framework we've summarized here (and will be teaching you in-depth throughout Ship 30 for 30).

All you have to do is type in what you want to write about, and voila! The AI-Powered EIG starts suggesting topics, headlines, and outlines for you—and you can easily save the ones you like and expand them into Atomic Essays (or Twitter Threads, or LinkedIn posts) later.

Pretty cool, right?

records.content:
Module Overview

Ahoy, and welcome to Onboarding Week Module #5!

In this module, we’re going to walk you through:

  • How to navigate our Ship 30 Skool community (and introduce yourself)

  • How to use our Rapid-Fire Intros feature to connect with likeminded Shippers

  • And a few other tips and suggestions for making the most out of your Ship 30 for 30 experience (from a community perspective)

Ready to dive?

Let’s do it!


🔹Lesson #1: Our Skool Community Feed

As we mentioned in the previous section, our “community feed” has 4 main categories where you can read other members’ posts and publish your own:

  • Announcements. Here, you find any ocasionnal updates from the Ship 30 for 30 team.

  • Introductions. From here, you can introduce yourself to the rest of the Ship 30 community—and read & engage with other member’s intros.

  • Wins. Inside this category, you can share your Digital Writing wins with the rest of the community.

  • Curriculum. Here, you can find all our curriculum assignment posts in one place. (These are posts where you can “submit” your assignments as you work your way through the Ship 30 curriculum!)

  • Discussions. Lastly, if you have any thoughts or questions you'd like to discuss with the rest of the Ship 30 community, you can share them here!

But now that you know all the ins and outs of how our Skool community is structured, it’s time to write and post your official Ship 30 introduction!


🔹Lesson #2: Introducing Yourself

How To Introduce Yourself To The Ship 30 Community

Click here to go over to our Introductions community feed (ideally open the link in a new tab) and create a new post introducing yourself.

Now, here are a few pro tips for crafting a clear introduction post (and make it easy for other likeminded shippers to connect & engage with you).

  1. Use an informative title for your introduction. That way, people can immediately know if you're interested in the same topics, from the same area, etc.

    Example: "Ahoy, I'm Dickie from Miami. I work full-time in financial services and I write about digital writing and digital leverage."

  2. For the body of your introduction, use this template:

  • Where are you based?

  • What are you currently working on?

  • What are 3 interests you plan on writing about?

  • What would a successful 30 days look like for you?

  • What’s your Twitter or Linkedin profile URL?


🔹Lesson #3: Making Your First Connections

Tip To Make Your First Ship 30 Connections

If making connections with other Shippers is a priority for you, we really encourage you to give the tips below a try so you can find a handful of folks you share interests with and start getting in touch with them!

Engage With Other Shippers’ Introductions

After introducing yourself, stay in the Introductions feed and scroll through it.

Find a few intros that resonate with you and leave them a note or send them a DM.

This is a great opportunity to find others with similar goals or interests, and start making new friends!

(Remember: You get out of Ship 30 what you put in!)

🔹Lesson #4: Onboarding Week Recap

Alas, we've reached the end of Onboarding Week and you've made it!

The hard part is over and everything is set up for you to write and publish every day for 30 days.

In just the past 5 days, you've:

  • Built your daily writing habit & set your constraints

  • Brainstormed 7 days of writing topics

  • Designed, created, and launched your Social Blog

  • Immersed yourself in a community of likeminded thinkers

  • And we built the foundation for a lifelong journey of writing and sharing your ideas online

Yes—we've thrown a lot at you this week.

And for good reason!

Because you've put in this work upfront, the next 30 days are going to be a breeze!

Well... not really.

Some days will be easy, and other days you will struggle. And that's okay! The beauty of Ship 30 for 30 is you have hundreds of others on the same journey as you, feeling the highs and lows, growing with one another.

In the beginning, your essays may take longer than you'd like. They may feel unfinished or unpolished. And again, that's okay! We promise that if you commit to writing and publishing for the next 30 days, you will look back and LAUGH at your first few essays because of how dramatically you've improved by the end.

Tomorrow is when the fun begins! You will get a true rush of euphoria hitting publish on that first essay. You'll feel the community momentum behind you seeing all of the others writing and publishing, overcoming fear and perfectionism as a collective community.

And we couldn't be any more excited to finally get your ship sailing.

So, to help you hit the water full speed (or to help you find your sea legs if you're not sure what to write about tomorrow!), we've put together a Day 1 prompt you can use.

Day 1 Writing Prompt

If you need a little help on your first essay, we encourage you to use the following prompt for tomorrow’s Atomic Essay #1:

  • Why did you join Ship 30 for 30?

  • What are you looking to write about?

  • What would a successful 30 days look like for you?

  • Reflect on where you are in your online writing journey and where you hope to be after 30 days

These 4 questions will help you set your expectations for the next 30 days, clarify your goals, and invite your friends and audience to follow along on your journey. And at the end of the 30 days, you'll be able to revisit it and it will help you reflect back on your journey!
